approaches.name: Plain rules
approaches.question: Do we even need AI?
approaches.idea: Read and check the quotation with plain Python rules.
approaches.wrong: Valid wording still causes cautious human referrals.

approaches.name: First AI attempt
approaches.question: Where does AI help?
approaches.idea: Ask one AI model to report the document facts.
approaches.right: Understands wording that fixed rules find difficult.
approaches.wrong: Right answers can arrive in the wrong shape.

approaches.name: Strict contract
approaches.question: Can it be dependable?
approaches.idea: Give the AI and code a strict output contract.
approaches.right: The same model returns more usable, structured facts.
approaches.wrong: Ambiguous and missing clauses still need a policy decision.

approaches.name: Reader + judge
approaches.question: Can it judge safely?
approaches.idea: One agent reads; a second reads the document and judges each rule.
approaches.right: Nine verdicts match after a policy change, with evidence.
approaches.wrong: Slower, with no code guard on approvals. Pack 01 still needs review.
